If you weren't around at the beginning of the season (about 90% of you!), I've written a program to keep track of Elo ratings for each team in the MLB. A quick explanation: 1500 is exactly average, higher is better, lower is worse. Whenever two teams play each other, a number of Elo points is transferred from the loser to the winner. That number is dictated by the margin of victory, difference in rating heading into the game, and who has home field advantage. Thus, a 1540 team squeaking out a 1-run victory over a 1470 team will earn very few points (probably about 1) compared to if the 1470 team had won by several runs (3-5 points). My methodology is borrowed from Nate Silver's old methodology from way back when, with minor differences. So here we are, halfway through the season:

The biggest success story of the first 81 games is probably Pittsburgh. They are up 9 ranks and 30 points since game 30 or so and are in great position to give St Louis a contest for control of the NL Central, the hardest division by 5 points.

The Phillies, on the other hand, are doing bad. They are projected to lose 107 games this year, picking up the "worst team in baseball" slack left after Houston lost at least 107 three times in the last five seasons. They singlehandedly drag the NL East division rating down by 19 points. Houston fans, for their part, are enjoying a well-deserved good season. Projected to finish 3 games behind the Angels, they have a great chance to get back to the postseason for the first time since 2005 (or, at least, their first winning season since 2008).

I'll update the ratings every 10 or 20 games through the rest of the season as division races start to gear up.

I've been researching a lot about Solaire, the God of War and the Lord of Sunlight, Gwyn. I've found a lot inconsistencies that make me doubt if Solaire is the person we think he is.

"I am Solaire of Astora, an adherent to the Lord of Sunlight."

The first thing that Solaire says to us, a warrior from Astora, a Gwyn enthusiast, if you will, yet, was it not the God of War who created the Warriors of the Sunlight Covenant, as it is said in the item description of the Sunlight Medal?:

"This faintly warm medal, engraved with the symbol of the Sun, is the ultimate honour, awarded to show those who summon the Warrior of Sunlight and complete a goal. The symbol represents Lord Gwyn's firstborn, who lost his deity status and was expunged from the annals. But the old God of War still watches closely over his warriors."

Then we have the description of The Great Lightning Spear:

"Miracle passed down to those bound by the Warrior of Sunlight covenant. Hurl giant lightning spear. The weapon of the God of War, who inherited the sunlight of Lord Gwyn, but had respect only for arms, and nothing else.

So it seems that the God of War did not care for the power of sunlight (the power of the Lord Souls), yet Solaire seeks "the sun", which is most likely a "code name" ,if you will, for the power of the Lord Souls. Solaire has also painted the symbol of the Sun on his armor, even though it's powerless. Now you could say that he's just one big fanatic of Gwyn, but then why does he go to Lost Izalith? Sure, it could be because he is the chosen undead like us (drawn from the fact that you can summon him for the fight with the Bell Gargoyles and the fight with the Gaping Dragon), but I'm pretty sure he went there because of the Lord Soul of the Witch of Izalith (though it was held by The Bed of Chaos). He also has a bit of dialogue in which he questions the location of the "sun":

"I did not find my own sun, not in Anor Londo, nor in Twilight Blighttown. Where else might my sun be? Lost Izalith, or the Tomb of the Gravelord… ?"

In the end (If you kill the chaos maggots before Solaire reaches them), he goes to The Kiln of The First Flame, where he etches his summon sign on the ground for the last time, as he goes to battle Gwyn. The outcome of that battle that takes place in Solaire's world is unknown, though he most likely fails...
Solaire is not the person we think he is...
The Dark Souls tvtropes trivia page cites a dev interview stating that Solaire will go on to link the fire in his world if you beat Gwyn with him in coop.
Huh, wasn't it a fan theory? You learn something new every day!
